title: Conchiglie al Pesto
subtitle: Shell pasta with basil pesto and green beans
excerpt: The traditional Ligurian way to serve pesto: pasta shells with green beans and potato, tossed in a fresh basil pesto made with a pestle and mortar. The potato thickens the sauce; the green beans add texture. Much better than pesto on plain pasta.

recipe.sourceNotes: In Liguria, pesto is traditionally served with trofie pasta, green beans, and potatoes, all cooked together in the same pot. The potato and pasta cooking water loosen and bind the pesto into a proper sauce. This version uses conchiglie, which traps the pesto well in its shells, and the same technique of adding green beans and waxy potato to the pot. The pesto here is made by hand in a pestle and mortar, which gives a slightly rougher, more vibrant texture than a blender.

recipeTools.notes: For the pesto; a food processor also works.
For the pasta, beans, and potato.

content.text: The pesto should be made fresh and not cooked. It goes on at the end, tossed through the hot pasta off the direct heat. Cooking pesto turns it dark and bitter. The pasta water is important here: a generous splash keeps the pesto loose and helps it coat the pasta evenly rather than clumping.

Make the pesto: pound the garlic with a pinch of salt in the pestle and mortar. Add the pine nuts and pound to a rough paste. Add the basil leaves in batches, pounding each batch. Work in the parmesan, then stir in the olive oil. Taste and adjust salt. Alternatively, blitz all in a food processor.

Bring a large pan of heavily salted water to a boil. Add the potato cubes and cook for 5 minutes. Add the conchiglie and cook for 8 minutes. Add the green beans and cook for a further 3 to 4 minutes until the pasta is al dente and the beans are just tender.

Reserve 150 ml of pasta water before draining. Drain and return the pasta, potato, and beans to the warm pan. Remove from the heat. Spoon in the pesto and a splash of pasta water. Toss well, adding more water to loosen as needed. Serve immediately.
